newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo's Trepca signs $220 mln export deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo's Trepca signs $220 mln export deal - paper.

text.p: Yugoslavia's metals giant Trepca of Kosovska Mitrovica and Trafigura from the United States have signed a $220 million deal involving lead and zinc exports, the Belgrade daily Politika reported on Friday.

"The new deal with the American company will enable Trepca even greater modernisation of equipment in all its plants, and thus greater productivity and better quality," Politika quoted Trepca general manager Novak Bjelic as saying.

Under the three-year contract signed on October 1, Trepca will import 150,000 tonnes of lead and zinc concentrates and export 20,000 tonnes each of refined lead and electrolytic zinc to the U.S. company per year.
The value of annual exports is around $76.3 million.
Trepca first signed a deal with Trafigura worth $30 million in early June, which was completed in four months.

"Trepca opened its doors to the U.S. market even before sanctions were removed," Bjelic said, referring to a U.N. imposed trade embargo on rump Yugoslavia lifted late on Tuesday after more than four years.
The complex introduced a revitalisation programme last February which restarted production after a virtual three-year standstill.
By early September, the value of Trepca's production had reached $1 billion.
"Only through fresh money from western companies can Trepca raise its production and exports," Politika quoted Bjelic as saying.
Rudarsko Metarlurski Kombinat Trepca merges 14 lead and zinc mines and 14 factories into the country's biggest metals complex, employing some 11,500 people.
